definition: A texture segregation task is a visual test in which a person responds to differences in patterned surfaces while brain activity is recorded. In the source, it is used to examine early visual-cortex input and the functioning of recurrent connections in the visual cortical system.

reasons: The definition says the task is “a visual test in which a person responds to differences in patterned surfaces,” but the provided packet text only states that ERPs were measured “during a texture segregation task” and does not describe what participants do or that stimuli are patterned surfaces requiring responses.
The definition’s claim that it examines “early visual-cortex input” is not stated in the packet; the packet only specifies that the C1 component was used to index afferent activity of V1.

The definition’s claim about “the functioning of recurrent connections” is only partially supported: the packet says the “texture negativity wave” provided “a measure for the integrity of recurrent connections,” but it does not directly support wording like “functioning.”

Because the definition contains at least one key substantive element not supported by the packet (participant responding to patterned-surface differences), it is not defensible under the provided-source constraint.
